method: Power Atlas investigative categories applied internationally. Original Power Atlas research is not recast as foreign evidence. Cases here use dated independent international primary sources.
publicationStatus: source-attributed curated research; new cross-source entity hypotheses are NOT published or confirmed
dataCoverage: Selected regulator cases and official country-level surveys, not a comprehensive country or corporate universe.
rules: Market concentration ≠ established consumer price impact
Donation/lobbying ≠ government corruption or quid pro quo
Household cost figures ≠ local market rent
Cross-country metrics must retain year, unit and denominator
Review required before cross-case causal assertions

domains.title: Political money
domains.short: Follow donors, lobbying and public decisions
domains.explain: Compare disclosure of campaign funding, lobbyist activity and policy outcomes. Report funding totals and legislation separately; never imply a donation bought a decision.

domains.title: Corporate ownership
domains.short: Identify legal control, subsidiaries and beneficial owners
domains.explain: Join entity identifiers and dated registry filings. A company number, LEI or beneficial-owner filing needs its issuing jurisdiction and as-of date.

domains.title: Market concentration
domains.short: Trace competition and who has negotiating power
domains.explain: Compare regulatory market definitions and evidence of competition, markups, bargaining power or antitrust findings. A market share is not an estimate of its effect on a household bill.

domains.title: Consumer protection
domains.short: Examine complaints, pricing and regulatory remedies
domains.explain: Separate studies, allegations, formal findings, settlements and remedies. Do not infer that historical conduct remains active.

domains.title: Banking & bailouts
domains.short: Track misconduct, public support and accountability
domains.explain: Link bank supervisors, resolution authorities, state aid and regulatory actions. A fine is not the same as restitution, consumer harm, taxpayer losses or net bank profit.

domains.title: Public procurement
domains.short: Follow state budgets, contractors and awards
domains.explain: Match public contract IDs to company registry IDs, distinguish bids from awards and obligations from paid invoices, and compare winners with competing bidders.

domains.title: Household costs
domains.short: Compare essential prices with local incomes
domains.explain: Use household survey definitions and years. Official poverty, household costs, CPI inflation and market rent are separate measures; no invented causal splits.

domains.title: Public accountability
domains.explain: Compare de-jure safeguards with actual practice using official audit and integrity criteria. Do not call an integrity gap proof that a country or office is corrupt.

cases.title: Seven housebuilders accept binding competition commitments
cases.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority closed its investigation by accepting commitments from seven builders over concerns about sensitive information exchange.
cases.whatProven: The final commitments restrict certain exchanges of sales-price information and require compliance measures; the builders agreed to pay £100 million across UK affordable-housing programmes.
cases.notEstablished: The CMA made no decision that the Competition Act was infringed, nor did it quantify the impact on individual home prices.

cases.title: Australian supermarket inquiry documents concentrated grocery markets
cases.statusLabel: Regulator market inquiry · not a fine
cases.summary: The ACCC's final supermarket inquiry examined consumer experience, retail competition, pricing, supply-chain relationships and supplier bargaining power.
cases.whatProven: The ACCC found problems with competition and pricing transparency and published 20 recommendations to improve consumer and supplier outcomes.
cases.notEstablished: The market-wide inquiry is not a court conviction or a finding that every retailer committed unlawful conduct.

cases.title: EU finds Apple in breach of Digital Markets Act anti-steering rule
cases.summary: The Commission found Apple's app distribution rules restricted developers' ability to inform consumers about alternative purchasing offers.
cases.whatProven: A formal European Commission non-compliance decision and a €500 million fine were announced on 23 April 2025.
cases.notEstablished: This does not establish any specific individual's damages or whether every subsequent challenge or appeal has concluded.

cases.title: EU finds Meta in breach of user-choice provisions
cases.summary: The Commission found Meta's consent arrangements did not give users a compliant choice of less-personal-data use under the DMA.
cases.whatProven: A formal non-compliance decision and a €200 million fine were announced in April 2025. The Commission subsequently described Meta's proposed alternative ad model.
cases.notEstablished: A regulatory fine does not measure individual compensation, all privacy harms, or the company's present compliance status.

cases.title: FCA fines Barclays for failures in financial-crime controls
cases.summary: The FCA imposed penalties on Barclays Bank UK PLC and Barclays Bank PLC for separate weaknesses managing financial-crime risks.
cases.whatProven: The regulator issued final notices for failures involving client-money account checks and banking relationships; it also disclosed a separate voluntary payment to affected WealthTek clients.
cases.notEstablished: The £42 million in fines is not a verified amount stolen, refunded, or paid by taxpayers; unrelated criminal defendants must not be conflated with the banks.

cases.title: UK government bond trading: competition decisions against banks
cases.metricLabel: Fines agreed by four settling banks
cases.summary: The CMA issued decisions on exchanges of sensitive information by traders at banks concerning UK government bonds in 2009–2013.
cases.whatProven: The CMA reported five infringement decisions and fines agreed by four settling banks totalling £104.46 million.
cases.notEstablished: The amount is not a proxy for all trading profits, market-wide investor losses or public debt-service costs; distinguish each bank's case.

cases.title: EU App Store music-streaming anti-steering decision
cases.summary: The Commission ruled that app distribution restrictions unlawfully prevented music-streaming developers from informing iOS users about cheaper offers outside the App Store.
cases.whatProven: The European Commission announced an antitrust infringement finding and fine exceeding €1.8 billion.
cases.notEstablished: This decision is legally distinct from the Commission's 2025 Digital Markets Act €500 million decision; appeals and present compliance require separate checks.

cases.title: FCA finds poor access to no-fee basic bank accounts
cases.metricLabel: Mystery-shop experiences rated poor or very poor
cases.summary: The FCA reported poor practices preventing some consumers facing hardship from easily obtaining a basic bank account.
cases.whatProven: The regulator published a mystery-shop review and said nine banks committed to changes.
cases.notEstablished: This is not a claim that one-third of all bank customers were denied accounts, nor a penalty against every bank.

cases.title: EU households experiencing housing-cost overburden
cases.metricLabel: EU 2025 share of population over the housing-cost threshold
cases.summary: In 2025, an estimated 7.7% of the EU population lived in households spending more than 40% of disposable household income on housing costs net of housing allowances.
cases.whatProven: Eurostat's EU-SILC household survey measures the rate using an explicit, internationally consistent threshold and survey year.
cases.notEstablished: This is not an advertised one-bedroom rent, a poverty cutoff, or a demonstrated causal effect of property ownership or government policy.

cases.title: Implementation lags written integrity safeguards
cases.summary: OECD integrity indicators report that members' integrity regulations score around 63% on relevant criteria, while practical implementation scores around 44%.
cases.whatProven: A documented cross-country difference between de-jure safeguards and practice under the OECD's own criteria.
cases.notEstablished: This is not an individual country's score, a probability of bribery or a ranking of corruption.
cases.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development

cases.title: Extractive-sector government revenue and company disclosures
cases.statusLabel: Multi-country reporting database · not a case finding
cases.metricLabel: Countries covered by the new database
cases.summary: EITI launched a searchable data resource linking oil, gas and mining company disclosures, state revenues, sector production and exports.
cases.whatProven: The international initiative reports coverage of more than $3.6 trillion in government revenues and 3,900 reporting entities across more than 55 countries; these are database coverage indicators.
cases.notEstablished: The database's inclusion of a company is not a finding of financial misconduct, beneficial ownership secrecy, sanctions evasion or causation.

cases.title: Competition Tribunal orders Rogers to pay penalty over wireless marketing
cases.summary: Canada's Competition Tribunal ruled in favour of the Competition Bureau in a case involving the advertising of Rogers Infinite wireless plans.
cases.whatProven: The Tribunal ordered a C$15 million penalty over marketing unlimited-data claims despite significant speed reductions after usage thresholds, plus a corrective notice.
cases.notEstablished: A regulatory decision does not establish the exact losses suffered by individual subscribers; appellate status and the full reasons must be checked separately.

cases.title: Canadian consent agreement addresses sharing of fuel-sales data
cases.summary: The Competition Bureau reached a consent agreement concerning Kalibrate Market Intelligence, which distributed detailed gas-station sales information to industry participants.
cases.whatProven: The Bureau reported a consent agreement to address concerns that competitively sensitive station-level sales information could weaken gas station competition.
cases.notEstablished: The agreement does not determine the amount by which any consumer's gas bill increased; the price effect was not quantified as an observed national figure.

cases.title: Brazilian competition tribunal penalizes automotive-components cartel
cases.summary: CADE reported an antitrust ruling against Denso Corporation for participation in a cartel involving wiring harnesses and automotive electronic components.
cases.whatProven: Brazil's competition authority reported a tribunal conviction and fine exceeding 100 million Brazilian reais in June 2026.
cases.notEstablished: This is not a documented effect on individual repair bills or vehicle prices, and any court challenge would need its own current docket.
cases.publisher: Brazil · Administrative Council for Economic Defense (CADE)

cases.title: Brazilian rail procurement cartel — recommendation, not final judgment
cases.metricLabel: Total value of at-least-seven procurements examined
cases.summary: CADE's Superintendent General recommended convictions over alleged coordinated bidding for rail infrastructure projects.
cases.whatProven: Agency investigators described at least seven rail procurement procedures within the cases and formally recommended convictions.
cases.notEstablished: The R$9.7 billion is the procurement value under examination, NOT money stolen, proved damages, or a Tribunal-imposed fine. The Tribunal had not issued a final ruling in the cited release.

cases.title: Edible oils pricing case resolved through Tribunal-confirmed settlement
cases.metricLabel: Settlement amount; other public-interest commitments separate
cases.summary: South Africa's Competition Tribunal confirmed a settlement with Wilmar SA regarding alleged price coordination for edible oils and baking fats.
cases.whatProven: The Competition Commission reported a Tribunal-confirmed settlement, a R1 million payment and separately described public-interest and investment commitments.
cases.notEstablished: Wilmar settled without an admission of liability; this cannot be presented as a finding of the firm's guilt, nor as a measured impact on consumers' grocery bills.

housing.definition: housing costs exceed 40% of household disposable income net of housing allowances
housing.note: Selected EU 2025 values from the published national indicator. The graph is descriptive and cannot estimate the contribution of any firm or policy.

integrity.population: OECD country averages across defined regulatory and practice criteria
integrity.warning: This is a 19-percentage-point implementation gap in OECD aggregate criteria, not a country ranking or probability of bribery.

worldBankIndicators.label: Consumer price inflation
worldBankIndicators.reason: Broad price inflation, not household expenditure or local rent

worldBankIndicators.label: Unemployment
worldBankIndicators.reason: Not a measure of wage adequacy or economic insecurity

worldBankIndicators.label: Gini index
worldBankIndicators.reason: Surveys differ in year and definition; higher means more unequal
